correctness.rationale: In the cutoff coordinates 0<=a<=b<=n, the Euclidean square is the number of changed binary coordinates, |u|+|v|, and incomparability is uv<0. The nonnegative gaps (a,b-a,n-b) must simultaneously admit the shift (u,v-u,-v). The sum of their required lower bounds is max(|u|,|v|,|u-v|); after taking out these lower bounds, stars and bars gives B_n at that displacement. Dividing signed counts by two gives both shell formulas, with both axes comparable and no incomparable shell after k=n. As a separate check, represent a vertex by the sorted pair (a,b+1). Each incomparable unordered pair corresponds to one four-element subset of {0,...,n+1}, paired strictly outer-with-inner. Its distance is 2 plus the sum of two designated gaps among the five nonnegative gaps of the four-subset, which are uniform over compositions of n-2. The sum of the two gaps has the stated beta-binomial law (two gap components versus three remaining components), giving the moments including the degenerate n=2 case and the beta limit. For the comparable limit, B_n(L)=n²(1-L/n)_+²/2+O(n) uniformly; summing comparable displacements gives the integral with integrand (1-max(x,t-x))_+², and axes are lower order. Dividing shell counts by binom(N_n,2) and rescaling gives the comparable contribution (8/3)[(1-t/2)^3-(1-t)_+^3], plus the incomparable contribution 4t(1-t)^2 on (0,1). These give the stated densities, tail and limits of means by integration and bounded support.

value.rationale: The metric is canonical and the rectangle is an already studied distance model. Resolving shells by containment, rather than giving a further moment, identifies exactly where long chords can occur and gives distinct typical scales and tails for comparable and incomparable pairs. The result gives a fixed-width distributional benchmark not supplied by proportional-width asymptotics.
